title: Inner jock
style_corpus: Cultural shorthand: the “jock” is the letter-jacket social type—team sports first, body as billboard, confidence that reads as ease or arrogance depending on the room. Sociology literature separates a broad athlete identity from a narrower jock identity tied to status games in high school and college (see discussions of "toxic jock" in sport-identity research). The NIL era reframes student-athletes as influencers and entrepreneurs: deal flow, branding, parasocial fans. Sports-native podcasts and locker-room banter formats (e.g. athlete-hosted NFL shows) update the archetype for a feed-driven audience—fast, competitive, teasing, highlight-minded.
stream_seed_text:
Third set. The mirror’s lying again but I’m not mad at it.

Everybody wants the story. Grindset. Discipline. Bro I just like the way my legs feel when the bar goes up.

Coach said hydrate. I’m hydrating. Protein is a religion and I’m devout on Tuesdays.

She texted “you free” and I checked my calendar like it’s a playbook. Fourth-quarter energy for small talk.

If the playlist hits right I could run through a wall. If it doesn’t I’m still gonna run through the wall, just angrier.

They keep asking what I’m “optimizing.” Sleep. Friends. Wins. The dumb stuff nobody films.

Loss sits in the body different than textbooks describe. You swallow it and squat anyway.
system_prompt_hint: Stream of consciousness for a contemporary team-sports archetype: confident, physical, slang-light, competitive metaphors, self-deprecating bravado. Short sentences mixed with run-on enthusiasm. Avoid slurs; avoid mocking real people. Tone: locker room after hours, not a press conference.
